def gpx_fields_to_xml(instance: Any, tag: str, version: str,
    custom_attributes: Dict[str, str]={}, nsmap: Dict[str, str]={},
    prettyprint: bool=True, indent: str='', empty_body: bool=False) ->str:
    
    if not prettyprint:
        indent = ''
    
    # Get the appropriate fields for this version
    fields = instance.gpx_10_fields
    if version == '1.1':
        fields = instance.gpx_11_fields
    
    # Build attributes string
    attributes_str = ''
    if custom_attributes:
        for key, value in custom_attributes.items():
            attributes_str += f' {key}="{mod_utils.make_str(value)}"'
    
    # Build namespace declarations
    nsmap_str = ''
    if nsmap:
        for prefix, uri in nsmap.items():
            if prefix:
                nsmap_str += f' xmlns:{prefix}="{uri}"'
            else:
                nsmap_str += f' xmlns="{uri}"'
    
    # Build opening tag
    opening_tag = f'\n{indent}<{tag}{nsmap_str}{attributes_str}>'
    
    if empty_body:
        return opening_tag.replace('>', ' />').lstrip('\n')
    
    # Build content from fields
    content_parts = []
    
    for gpx_field in fields:
        if isinstance(gpx_field, str):
            # Handle path markers like "tag:dep1:dep2" or "/tag"
            skip, field_name = _check_dependents(instance, gpx_field)
            if skip:
                # Skip this field and its content
                continue
        else:
            # Serialize the field
            value = getattr(instance, gpx_field.name, None)
            field_xml = gpx_field.to_xml(value, version, nsmap=nsmap, 
                                        prettyprint=prettyprint, 
                                        indent=indent + '  ')
            if field_xml:
                content_parts.append(field_xml)
    
    # Build result
    if content_parts:
        content = ''.join(content_parts)
        closing_tag = f'\n{indent}</{tag}>'
        return opening_tag + content + closing_tag
    else:
        # Empty element
        return opening_tag.replace('>', ' />').lstrip('\n')
